Find a 1952 paper solving a modeling sub-problem
A researcher developing a model had Claude Code point them to a 1952 paper with a better steady-state solution than their time-dependent approach.
·
Nov 25, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
While developing a model, Ken Caldeira worked with Claude Code. It pointed him to a 1952 paper that solved one sub-problem with a steady-state solution. His own approach had been time-dependent. He then had to ask Claude separately for the citation to that solution method.
How it went
The steady-state solution from the 1952 paper was much better than his time-dependent approach. He says he wouldn't have known how to search for that paper. No numbers are given.
Worth knowing
Ask for the citation to the method explicitly, since Claude gave the idea first and the reference only when asked, so check it yourself.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I'm building a model of [describe your system and what it predicts], and I currently solve it with [your current approach, e.g. a time-dependent simulation]. Search for older or foundational papers, including pre-1980 work, that give a steady-state, analytical, or simpler solution to [the specific sub-problem]. Finish with a list of 3 to 5 candidate papers, each with citation, a two-sentence summary of its method, and how it could replace or improve my current approach.
Original source: https://bsky.app/profile/kencaldeira.com/post/3n35ev6qkac2q
